description: Switch on sign-in (Neon Auth) for this application now, while the project is still being written, so a login page is built and tested against the real thing instead of a library and a table of passwords of your own. The people who sign up are rows in a neon_auth schema of the application's own Postgres, so it makes the database first if there is none, and that counts against the plan's databases. Safe to call twice. Only for a project that has accounts: skip it otherwise, and skip it when the user already chose a service (Clerk, Auth0, Supabase Auth), or when the project connects to a database of its own: the answers are 409 own_auth and own_database. A 402 database_limit is not a rate limit, so do not retry, say what it says and let the user choose. If the call is refused or blocked, do not look for another route: tell the user. The cookie secret is not returned: call `auth_env_to_file` to put the variables in .env. In Next.js, install @neondatabase/auth and follow https://neon.com/docs/auth/quick-start/nextjs (a beta library, so that page is the source of truth for its code). Anywhere else it is Better Auth over HTTP at NEON_AUTH_BASE_URL: POST /sign-up/email and /sign-in/email, GET /get-session, and GET /token for a JWT that verifies against NEON_AUTH_JWKS_URL, every request carrying an Origin that is the application's own address. Localhost works while you build, and the platform registers the application's address and any custom domain itself. Sign-up and sign-in allow about nine attempts per ten seconds, then answer 429, so show a person a try-again message. Tell the user what was created and on which account.
name: auth_create
title: Switch on sign-in for the application's own users now
